expectations_used.clarify: Since there is no interviewer, pins down each part's contract from the statement and tests/cases files alone -- for instance that touching endpoints still merge in the booking windows, that a tile may not be reused within one trace, and that repeated values never extend a strictly increasing streak -- rather than guessing at a variant rule.
expectations_used.approach: Names a mechanism for each part before typing it -- sweeping the sorted bookings while extending a running window, backtracking across the tiles with a used-mark that clears on the way out, and tracking the best increasing run ending at each reading -- not merely naming a topic like dynamic programming.
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates the reasoning behind each part as it happens rather than going quiet across the ninety-minute session -- e.g. saying aloud why a booking window extends or closes, why a tile gets marked and unmarked, why a reading's streak length looks back only at smaller earlier readings -- so the trace explains the path across all three parts, not only the final code.
expectations_used.implement: Correctly handles the touching-endpoint case for the booking windows, the used-tile backtracking for the board trace, and the tie case where a repeated reading does not extend the increasing streak, matching the behavior exercised by tests/cases_part1.json, cases_part2.json, and cases_part3.json.
expectations_used.verify: Since this is a one-shot autograded set, runs the visible sample tests for every part and hand-checks a touching-endpoint booking case, a failed-trace tile case, and a repeated-reading case before submitting once, rather than submitting on first successful compile.
expectations_used.reflect: Can explain why sorting the bookings first makes one sweep enough, why the tile trace must undo its mark on every dead end, and why the reading streak needs the best-ending-here value at every earlier index -- not just a one-line 'it passed'.
